title: Statewide Boxing Day trading (NSW)
summary: The Retail Trading Amendment Act 2015 allowed shops statewide to open on Boxing Day if staffed only by people who freely elected to work (trial for 2015 and 2016); the Retail Trading Amendment (Boxing Day) Act 2017 removed the sunset.

instruments.title: Retail Trading Amendment (Boxing Day) Act 2017 No 45

commenced.what: Act commenced on assent (first statewide Boxing Day trading 26 Dec 2015)

direction_rationale: One extra trading day a year modestly increases retailers' ability to compete; effects on entry are likely small.
notes: Small treatment; best used as a placebo/robustness case rather than a headline estimate.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 14-15 October 2026 from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use. Primary commencement chosen on 15 October 2026 as the date the change described in the title took effect; confirm on review.

assessment.summary: Allowed shops across New South Wales to open on Boxing Day. One extra trading day a year: a small gain. The Productivity Commission has recommended removing trading hours restrictions altogether.

marks.reason: Longer permitted hours let retailers compete on convenience and give shoppers more choice.
